symptom: `alter page … set (showFooter: true, clearable: false) on <combobox>` stores PrimitiveValue "yes" / "no"; mx check passes and the client reads "yes" as false, so a bare `true` turns the property off
cause: setPluggableWidgetPropertyMut spelled every Go bool as yes/no regardless of the property's declared ValueType.Type, although Studio Pro and the widget template store a Boolean as true/false
insight: The literal's type is not the stored type: the spelling must come from the schema (propKindMap) the same way columnValueField already picks the value field. yes/no is real only as the keys of an Enumeration that declares them (the reporter's 17.5k-unit scan: 0 yes/no among 13k Boolean values, 2.1k among enumerations), so those keep taking a boolean and any other enumeration refuses one. A unit test named TestSetWidgetProperty_PluggableWidget had pinned "no" on a kindless fixture — the bug's spelling was the asserted contract. mx check accepts both spellings (0 errors on fixed and unfixed builds), so only the stored bytes show it
